The OlinkExperiment class

Source: R/AllClasses.R, R/OlinkExperiment.R
OlinkExperiment.Rd

The OlinkExperiment class is designed to represent Olink proteomics data. It inherits from the RangedSummarizedExperiment class and is used in the same manner: rows represent proteins while columns represent samples. In addition, the class supports storage of dimensionality reduction results (e.g., PCA, UMAP) via reducedDims.

Usage

OlinkExperiment(..., reducedDims = list())

Arguments

...

Arguments passed to the SummarizedExperiment constructor to fill the slots of the base class. In particular, the assays argument should be a list of matrices (or matrix-like objects) with one row per protein and one column per sample. Olink NPX values are conventionally stored in an assay named "NPX" (see npx), with the limit of detection in "LOD" (see lod) and raw protein counts in "PC" (see pcount).

reducedDims

A list of any number of matrix-like objects containing dimensionality reduction results, each of which should have the same number of rows as the output OlinkExperiment object (i.e., one row per sample).

Value

An OlinkExperiment object.

Details

In this class, rows should represent proteins while columns represent samples generated from Olink proteomics experiments.

As with any SummarizedExperiment derivative, different quantifications (e.g., NPX, LOD, protein counts) can be stored simultaneously in the assays slot, and row and column metadata can be attached using rowData and colData, respectively. Here, rowData is expected to contain protein-level annotation (e.g., OlinkID, UniProt, Panel, Assay) while colData is expected to contain sample-level annotation (e.g., SampleID, SubjectID, group, time point).

The extra arguments in the constructor (e.g., reducedDims) represent the main extension implemented in the OlinkExperiment class. This enables a consistent, formalized representation of the data structures commonly encountered during Olink data analysis.

An OlinkExperiment can also be created by coercing from a SummarizedExperiment or RangedSummarizedExperiment instance; see coerce,OlinkExperiment,SummarizedExperiment-method.

See also

reducedDims, for representation of dimensionality reduction results.

npx, lod and pcount, for Olink-specific named assay accessors.

?"OE-internals", for developer use.

Author

Lucas

Examples

nproteins <- 200
nsamples <- 20
set.seed(100)

# Simulated NPX and LOD matrices (proteins x samples)
npx_mat <- matrix(rnorm(nproteins * nsamples, mean = 5, sd = 1),
    nrow = nproteins, ncol = nsamples,
    dimnames = list(paste0("OID", seq_len(nproteins)),
        paste0("Sample", seq_len(nsamples))))
lod_mat <- matrix(0.5, nrow = nproteins, ncol = nsamples,
    dimnames = dimnames(npx_mat))

# Sample and protein annotation
colData_df <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(SampleID = colnames(npx_mat),
    Group = rep(c("case", "control"), each = nsamples / 2))
rowData_df <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(OlinkID = rownames(npx_mat),
    Panel = rep(c("Inflammation", "Cardiometabolic"), length.out = nproteins))

oe <- OlinkExperiment(
    assays = list(NPX = npx_mat, LOD = lod_mat),
    colData = colData_df,
    rowData = rowData_df
)
oe
#> class: OlinkExperiment 
#> dim: 200 20 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(2): NPX LOD
#> rownames(200): OID1 OID2 ... OID199 OID200
#> rowData names(2): OlinkID Panel
#> colnames(20): Sample1 Sample2 ... Sample19 Sample20
#> colData names(2): SampleID Group
#> reducedDimNames(0):

## coercion from SummarizedExperiment
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(NPX = npx_mat, LOD = lod_mat))
as(se, "OlinkExperiment")
#> class: OlinkExperiment 
#> dim: 200 20 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(2): NPX LOD
#> rownames(200): OID1 OID2 ... OID199 OID200
#> rowData names(0):
#> colnames(20): Sample1 Sample2 ... Sample19 Sample20
#> colData names(0):
#> reducedDimNames(0):

## coercion to a SummarizedExperiment
as(oe, "SummarizedExperiment")
#> class: SummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 200 20 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(2): NPX LOD
#> rownames: NULL
#> rowData names(0):
#> colnames(20): Sample1 Sample2 ... Sample19 Sample20
#> colData names(2): SampleID Group
